title: Black Holes & Cosmology
blurb: The Big Bang, dark matter and the strangest objects out there

questions.question: What is a region of space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape?
questions.fact: A black hole forms when a huge amount of mass is squeezed into a tiny space.

questions.question: The leading theory for how the universe began is called the…
questions.fact: The name 'Big Bang' was coined in 1949 by Fred Hoyle — who actually doubted the theory.

questions.question: The 'point of no return' around a black hole is called the…
questions.fact: Once anything crosses the event horizon, every possible path leads further inward.

questions.question: Which scientist developed the general theory of relativity?
questions.fact: Einstein published general relativity in 1915, describing gravity as the curving of spacetime.

questions.question: Roughly how old is the universe?
questions.fact: 4.6 billion years is the age of our Solar System — the universe is three times older.

questions.question: In 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of…
options: The black hole in galaxy M87
The black hole at the Milky Way's centre
questions.fact: The image of the Milky Way's own black hole, Sagittarius A*, followed in 2022.

questions.question: What is the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way called?
questions.fact: Sagittarius A* has a mass of about 4 million Suns.

questions.question: What is the faint microwave 'afterglow' of the Big Bang called?
questions.fact: It was discovered by accident in 1964 by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson.

questions.question: Hawking radiation suggests that black holes can slowly…
questions.fact: For a black hole the mass of the Sun, evaporating would take far longer than the current age of the universe.

questions.question: Who showed in 1929 that distant galaxies are moving away from us?
questions.fact: Hubble's observations were key evidence that the universe is expanding.

questions.question: The stretching of objects falling into a black hole is nicknamed…
questions.fact: It happens because gravity pulls much harder on the near end of an object than the far end.

questions.question: About what fraction of the universe is ordinary matter (atoms)?
questions.fact: Roughly 27% is dark matter and about 68% is dark energy.

questions.question: Gravitational waves were first directly detected in 2015 by which observatory?
questions.fact: The discovery earned the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.question: The theoretical point of infinite density at a black hole's centre is the…
questions.fact: Physicists expect a future theory of quantum gravity to explain what really happens there.

questions.question: Approximately how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.fact: Light could circle Earth about 7.5 times in a single second.

questions.question: What is thought to be driving the accelerating expansion of the universe?
questions.fact: The accelerating expansion was discovered in 1998 and won the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.question: The first gravitational waves ever detected came from the merger of…
questions.fact: The two black holes were about 29 and 36 times the Sun's mass, 1.3 billion light-years away.

questions.question: The radius of a non-rotating black hole's event horizon is named after…
questions.fact: Schwarzschild found the solution in 1916 — while serving on the front lines in World War I.

questions.question: The Hubble constant describes…
options: How fast the universe is expanding
The mass of the Milky Way
questions.fact: Different measurement methods disagree on its value — a puzzle called the 'Hubble tension'.

questions.question: Dark matter was strongly supported by observations that…
questions.fact: Vera Rubin's measurements of galaxy rotation in the 1970s were crucial evidence.
